races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jack Sparowe
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a win at Goodwood over 10f, handled Good ground well but this Standard AW surface produced a 6th on their last visit over 12f; a true hold-up horse operating off a slow pace in a race where the rear is congested, meaning its natural position is compromised and the chance is tempered.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of his last three starts — third last time out, and a winner three starts back — Jack Sparowe brings solid recent consistency, though 61 days off the track is a slight fitness query; he has experience over today's trip and going, and carries 137 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Booziebrunch
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with front-running profile who has won over 10f on Good and holds a solid record as a pace-setter; T14 of 0/6 for trainer Woods is worth noting, but the tactical role here is clear and an uncontested lead on Standard AW at Lingfield over 1m2f is a significant advantage.
runners_data.comment: Booziebrunch arrives on the back of a win two starts ago and was runner-up last time out, showing consistent form that marks him out as the one to beat here; he has run over today's distance and going before, and his rating of 85 heads the field.

runners_data.name: Eagles Attire
runners_data.note: 101 days off the track is a significant concern for a three-year-old who has shown only a best of 6th in three starts, all on Good or Soft ground; no AW experience makes the Standard surface an unknown and Daniel Muscutt will need to find improvement from a horse with limited exposed form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and absent for 101 days, Eagles Attire returns carrying 134 lb from stall five looking exposed on these figures — ranked eighth of nine — and he has plenty to prove after that long break.

runners_data.name: Barbury Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and 12f on Good at three, showing versatility over the trip, but has just one AW start (11th at 7f on Standard) and the surface switch is unproven; Harry Vigors's 5lb claim could be valuable in a tight handicap if the horse handles the Polytrack.
runners_data.comment: Barbury Boy won two of his last five starts, including a victory two runs back, and has experience of both today's trip and going — he arrives fresh on 40 days off carrying 134 lb from stall three. The main concern is that seventh last time out will need explaining.

runners_data.name: Alice De Clare
runners_data.note: Landed a hat-trick of wins over 10f on Good in strong form, with Callum Shepherd booked and trainer Fanshawe among the most active stables over the fortnight; the drop to AW Standard from a Good-ground sequence is the one query, with only 0W0P from three AW starts in her history.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last six starts show she can find the winner's enclosure, but ranked seventh of nine on our figures and a speed rating of 61 make her hard to fancy against this field; 56 days off adds a fitness query, though she has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Turku
runners_data.note: Fitted with a visor, which is worth watching for a positive behavioural response, but the form string of 654-0 on Standard AW suggests this surface has consistently found them out; Simon & Ed Crisford are in strong form (T14: 7/22) and that stable confidence is the main reason to give a second look.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts with an unplaced effort the most recent of those, Turku is ranked last on our figures here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a trainer firing at 32% over the past fortnight offers some slim hope.

runners_data.name: Kaaranah
runners_data.note: The standout profile in the race on course-and-distance form, with four wins from twelve at Lingfield over 10f on Standard AW and top weight of 142lbs indicating the handicapper's respect; John Butler's stable is running at 5/18 over the past fortnight and Jack Callan takes the ride, combining course mastery with a barn in form.
runners_data.comment: Kaaranah arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, but the fifth and sixth earlier in this sequence suggest he's not infallible, and 142 lb is a stern test of his current momentum.

runners_data.name: City Of God
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and won over 8f on Standard AW at this course, but has been beaten in both subsequent starts and steps up in trip to 10f here for the first time since that win; Finley Marsh is an inexperienced claimer and the 69-day absence adds an element of uncertainty to a horse with a patchy recent record.
runners_data.comment: City Of God showed smart form when winning four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going underlines his claims here; the concern is that he has been off the track for 69 days and returns to form is the key question.

runners_data.name: Barry's Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Standard AW and has placed twice at this sort of level, but career best form has come over 8f and the step to 10f at Lingfield — a galloping AW circuit — is a genuine question; the 38-day absence is fine and Denis Coakley's limited trainer-14-day strike rate (0/4) offers no particular stable confidence boost.
runners_data.comment: Barry's Boy shaped well when second last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a genuine threat at 141 lb from stall six; the nine-finish two starts back is the one blot to dismiss.

races.paceDynamic: Booziebrunch is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push them off the lead, should control tempo from the outset at Lingfield's AW circuit over 1m2f. Alice De Clare, Turku, and Kaaranah will all press for prominent positions just off the leader, creating a compact early order but not a truly contested lead — the pace should be honest rather than scorching on Standard going. Jack Sparowe is a natural hold-up horse redistributed into the midfield map position because the field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can accommodate; Jack Sparowe, City Of God, and Barry's Boy are all genuine closers who will need to make ground in the straight. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a controlled, sustainable pace with prominent types tracking close — strongly favours horses with good tactical speed who can sit handily and quicken from an organised position, placing the prominent-to-midfield profile at a premium over deep closers who may find the pace insufficiently strong to create the gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Booziebrunch Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Booziebrunch leads uncontested and sets a fair but manageable gallop that suits those tracking within two lengths.
scenarios.body: Booziebrunch dictates from the front and, with no horse willing to match strides early, controls the race throughout the 1m2f trip and is hard to peg back on a tight AW circuit; horses tracking in prominent positions — particularly Kaaranah and Alice De Clare — have the first opportunity to challenge and are ideally placed when the race ignites from the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to stop Booziebrunch but a prominent tracker picks up sharply in the straight.
scenarios.body: Kaaranah — with four wins at this course and distance on Standard AW — is ideally positioned to exploit any fade from Booziebrunch, while Alice De Clare's hat-trick of wins over 10 furlongs on Good ground suggests she has the quality to assert once Booziebrunch is headed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and leave genuine closers with daylight in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Barry's Boy and City Of God are natural hold-up types who could produce a late run if the gallop is genuinely strong, but both face an uphill task given Lingfield AW favours those who can travel; Jack Sparowe, though racing out of preferred position, remains a course-and-distance placed horse who could make up ground if the gaps materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Dash
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is falsely slow and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: In a messy dash for home, form figures become less reliable and unexposed or improving types like Barbury Boy — who has shown a turn of foot in small fields on Good ground — could surprise, while Eagles Attire at longer odds might find a slow-run race playing to a one-paced closer profile; however this scenario is the least likely given Booziebrunch's front-running profile.

watchPoints.text: Kaaranah's weight of 142lbs is the highest in the field — watch whether it is sent up to track Booziebrunch promptly from stall, as any sluggish start could compromise its ability to settle in the prominent position its course record demands.
Booziebrunch is the lone front-runner and any significant drift in the market or a slow break from stall could allow Alice De Clare or Turku to steal the lead and entirely reshape the pace dynamic.

Turku wears a visor for the first time or as a headgear change — watch the pre-race behaviour and early strides; if the horse jumps sharply and travels with more purpose than recent efforts suggest, it becomes a live danger at a bigger price.

Eagles Attire has had 101 days off and has no AW experience — watch the paddock for condition and how it handles the surface in the early furlongs, as a well-backed debut on Polytrack would signal trainer confidence worth noting.

Jack Sparowe and Barry's Boy are both natural hold-up horses who will need the pace to be genuinely strong to get into the race late — if Booziebrunch sets only a modest gallop, monitor whether either is able to make meaningful headway before the home turn or whether they are effectively out of the race by that point.

races.name: Follow @AtTheRaces On X EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Emilies 21st Birthday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Quick Quasar
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with a recent win over C&D in identical Standard conditions; Archie Watson handler is well-respected here, and with 13 rivals and no pace duel, she dictates every fraction — the key question is whether OR 65 is a burden over 7f.|
runners_data.comment: Quick Quasar has run over today's trip and going, rates level with his official mark, and a return to form isn't impossible off a 13-day break — but a winner just once in his last six starts and a trainer firing at only 3% are real concerns.

runners_data.name: Midnight's Dream
runners_data.note: Holds up by nature and shows three places from 15 starts at the trip, but with a cluster of genuine closers needing the rear, she is effectively racing in unfamiliar midfield territory which blunts her typical late-running profile; drop to OR 58 is the mild positive.|
runners_data.comment: Midnight's Dream has been placed in each of his last three starts — third last time out, and a second two starts back — and has experience over today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that he remains yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Wind Summer
runners_data.note: 136-day break is the standout concern here — last ran over 10f on the same surface and has placed at this trip before, but the ring rustiness combined with a bumper Lingfield layoff makes her hard to trust at short prices without a prep run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and rated 13th of 13 on our figures, Wind Summer faces a stiff task here; 136 days off the track doesn't help, though he has run over today's trip and going before and his second two starts back shows he can compete on a good day.

runners_data.name: Francisco
runners_data.note: Two wins from 15 AW starts suggest he is capable, and his best form has come on this surface at 7f, but his natural hold-up style is squeezed into midfield in this race shape — Charlie Tucker's claim is a useful weight-saver, though the positional compromise is a real cost.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last three starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Francisco is hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going before; the 134 lb burden won't help, though a win four starts back shows he can find the line.

runners_data.name: Chelio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who placed twice at this trip on Standard going and is the most likely horse to take up a position directly behind Quick Quasar; the 69-day break is a mild flag, but Denis Coakley horses often reappear ready.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but Chelio does show a runner-up finish last time out and has run over today's trip and going before; 69 days off the track is a fitness query, and a mark of 61 leaves him with little margin for error from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Blue Samuna
runners_data.note: Six runners from 13 in the midfield group means positional traffic is a genuine risk; no wins or places from six starts on Standard going is a damning sim-going record, and Robert Havlin will need everything to go right.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than fourth in recent starts, Blue Samuna ranks 12th of 13 on our figures and looks up against it here; she has run over today's trip and going, and 13 days between runs suggests she is at least fit.

runners_data.name: Captive Beauty
runners_data.note: Has already placed at 7f on this surface in her most recent run, and David Probert is a strong booking at Lingfield — a prominent profile suits this race shape, making her one to monitor from the outside as a place candidate.|
runners_data.comment: Captive Beauty shaped with promise when second last time out, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but a winless run in her last four starts and a ranking of ninth of thirteen suggest she faces a stiff task from stall 11 off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: My Dad Tom
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been over 5-6f, making this 7f trip a step into the unknown for a horse whose pedigree hints at stamina but whose race experience doesn't confirm it; natural hold-up style displaced to midfield in this congested race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, My Dad Tom nevertheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and his 64 rating suggests he's worth more than his official mark of 58 — the risk is replicating that elusive fourth as his best recent effort.

runners_data.name: Oxford Circus
runners_data.note: Fourteen-runner finishes at Goodwood tell a bleak story, and his one AW win came over 5f — both the trip extension and the Standard-going record (1W from 10) suggest he is up against it, despite a low OR of 51.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 11th of 13 on our figures, Oxford Circus has been largely out of the frame in recent outings; 64 days off the track does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Lerwick
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a recent win at 8f on Good going, and his 9-day turnaround is quick; carrying 146lbs top weight is the significant burden, and Hope Regan's 7lb claim only partially offsets it — better suited to a race with a stronger pace to close into.|
runners_data.comment: Lerwick bounced back to winning ways last time out and, with experience of today's trip and going, he arrives here in excellent heart just nine days on; carrying 146 lb from stall 12, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Breeze
runners_data.note: One AW win at 7f at Lingfield already on his record and has placed twice in recent form; Finley Marsh is an able rider, and a prominent to midfield style fits this race shape well — the 24-day break is manageable for this well-exposed six-year-old.|
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Breeze has placed in each of his last two starts, including a win four starts back, though a ninth three starts back tempers optimism; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 141 lb is a stern ask from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Split Elevens
runners_data.note: Most consistent horse in the field with two wins and seven places from 13 AW starts at this exact trip and surface — Jack Callan knows him well and the 46-day break is the only mild concern; a genuine hold-up type who needs a stronger pace than this to deliver his best.|
runners_data.comment: Split Elevens brings distance and going experience plus a win three starts back, but he was fourth last time out and 46 days off the track raises a fitness query; carrying 138 lb from stall one, he looks a midfield prospect at best.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Three wins from nine AW starts is a strong strike rate, but all of that form is over 5-6f — stepping to 7f is uncharted territory, and his natural hold-up style is repositioned to midfield here, meaning he cannot reproduce his typical last-to-first style on a longer trip.|
runners_data.comment: Elvetham bounced back to winning form last time out, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but a sixth two starts back tempers enthusiasm, and carrying 138 lb from stall 2 is the reality he faces here.

races.paceDynamic: Quick Quasar is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is almost certain to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop over Lingfield's 7f AW straight. Chelio, Captive Beauty, Spirit Of Breeze, and Oxford Circus will push forward into prominent positions just behind, creating a compact early order with the pace controlled rather than injected. The large contingent of nominal hold-up types — Midnight's Dream, Francisco, My Dad Tom, and Elvetham — are redistributed to midfield on the map because there is no room for all of them at the rear in a race this shape; their true closing ability will be compromised by the position they are forced to settle in. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently behind a single, unchallenged front-runner and produce a sustained run from 2f out, as the moderate, uncontested pace is unlikely to generate the gap that true closers need to deliver late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quasar Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar leads unchallenged and the prominent trackers kick past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Quick Quasar sets a metronomic tempo that suits horses sitting just off the pace, and with no rival forcing a true test, those tracking in second or third position have the most energy to deploy in the straight. Spirit Of Breeze and Split Elevens, both proven at 7f on this surface and capable of prominent racing, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Quasar Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar's lead is never seriously threatened and the pace is too slow to reel her in.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied early, Quick Quasar dictates every fraction and the field never gets close enough to mount a meaningful challenge in the straight. At OR 65 on a surface and trip she has already won at in recent form, the front-runner's chance of simply staying on is real.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar goes too slow and the field bunches, allowing a late run from the rear to cut through.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace occasionally creates a falsely run race where hold-up horses find daylight late, but in this field those types are forced wide in midfield and lack the true rear-running setup to deliver that burst. Split Elevens and Lerwick, the most genuine closers with strong Standard-going form at the trip, are best positioned to capitalise if chaos breaks out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Disruption
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar's early fractions are misjudged or the field surges to challenge, causing a messy, non-typical shape.
scenarios.body: A breakdown in the expected shape could allow a prominent horse to nick it from a chaotic finish, but this is a low-probability outcome given Watson's record at producing well-judged rides from the front. Spirit Of Breeze's course form and Chelio's place record at the trip make them the safest each-way profiles if something unexpected unfolds.

watchPoints.text: Quick Quasar's pace — if William Cox goes too steadily through the first 3f, the entire field will be racing in a bunch approaching the 2f pole, which could turn the straight into a sprint where her front-running advantage evaporates.

Split Elevens is the most proven horse at this exact trip and surface (13 AW runs, 2W, 7P) but needs a genuine pace to close into — watch whether the slow early fractions leave him too far back to reach the principals.
Lerwick carries 146lbs top weight and turns around in just 9 days — if the weight takes its toll in the closing stages, the race outcome changes significantly for the prominent horses tracking him.

Spirit Of Breeze has existing course and distance form on the All-Weather — watch his early position; if Finley Marsh gets him up into second or third early, he is a live contender to go past a tiring front-runner.

Francisco and Midnight's Dream are both mapped to midfield despite being true hold-up horses — if either jockey sends them forward early against their natural style, it could compress the midfield and create traffic problems for the entire chasing pack.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Porfin
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer in this grade with strong Standard-going form (12/15 sim-going), races over a familiar 6f trip, and Phil McEntee's 0/5 T14 is the one concern, but Grace McEntee's partnership and the horse's record of placing regularly makes it a genuine each-way contender in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in defeat but knocking loudly at the door, Porfin has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 53 makes him one to reckon with from stall seven — the worry is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Roman Spring
runners_data.note: Back quickly after just 5 days, which warrants monitoring for freshness, and sim-going form (3/15) is modest; races prominently and will compete for the early rail position behind Pure Passion, but the quick turnaround and weak Standard-going profile is a significant caution.
runners_data.comment: Roman Spring shaped with promise when fourth two starts back and third four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts and a swift five-day turnaround may blunt his edge under 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Zaltalla
runners_data.note: David Probert takes the ride for Gary & Josh Moore (4/23 T14), and this hold-up horse has strong Standard-going credentials (11/15); drops back to 6f from recent 7f/8f runs which could suit a flat-track sprint, though getting clear from the hold-up berth without a strong pace is the key dependency.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second two starts back, Zaltalla arrives in decent nick after 22 days, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; yet to win in recent starts, but his profile of consistent placing makes him our pick from stall 2 carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 5-6f with strong form figures (132242), but this is genuinely a hold-up horse who will find itself pressed into a closer role given how many rear-of-field types are in this field — that positional compromise tempers its prospects in a steadily-run race.
runners_data.comment: My Mate Mackley has been placed four times in his last six starts — including second last time out — and has experience of today's distance and going, but ranked eighth of nine on our figures, he faces a stiff ask at these weights.

runners_data.name: Real Gold
runners_data.note: Four places from its last five on Standard going (0W4P) and a reliable hold-up type who shows consistent willingness to run on; like Zaltalla, depends on Pure Passion holding a decent tempo — Rachel Cook & John Bridger's yard is 0/9 in the T14 window.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without threatening the principals, Real Gold has posted four thirds in her recent starts but is winless in her last six, and her latest seventh checks the momentum; she has run over today's trip and going before, though carrying 131 lb from stall one adds another test.

runners_data.name: Ridger
runners_data.note: Raw record (699) tells a blunt story — three runs, no placing, including two 9ths on this course; tagged as fading in the finish and the T14 is 3/13, but that trainer activity contrasts with a horse yet to show it can compete at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a pair of ninths his most recent efforts, Ridger looks hard to fancy here — ranked bottom on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a manageable 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Pure Passion
runners_data.note: The race's sole leader and therefore the controlling influence on pace; won over 5f on Good, unproven at 6f in Standard, and carries top weight (137lbs) with a 7lb claimer in Chloe Lyons — the weight concession and distance extension are the two legitimate queries around an otherwise tactically well-placed runner.
runners_data.comment: Pure Passion won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but her official mark of 54 sits above our rating of 50, and her form before that win was patchy — she arrives with claims but also questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Dr Ali
runners_data.note: Two career wins on Standard (2W in sim-going), races for veteran handler J.R. Jenkins (0/3 T14), and wears a visor; a natural hold-up horse who will be shuffled toward midfield by the traffic of similarly-styled rivals, reducing its effectiveness unless the pace is surprisingly strong.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and a winner six starts back, Dr Ali brings distance and going experience to the table and our rating has him narrowly at the head of the rankings — though the quick five-day turnaround is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Global Effort
runners_data.note: Returning after a 150-day absence — a significant flag — and has run exclusively over 5f recently, so stepping to 6f is an untested stretch; Phil McEntee's 0/5 T14, combined with the long layoff and natural hold-up style that will be squeezed in this field, makes this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 150 days, Global Effort has plenty to prove stepping back in, and his official mark of 45 leaves little margin for error — experience over today's trip and going is about his only genuine positive.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Passion is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, should settle into an uncontested rhythm from the gates on this flat Lingfield AW 6f — a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a frantically-run race. Porfin and Roman Spring will push for prominent positions behind her, while the bulk of the field — Zaltalla, My Mate Mackley, Real Gold, Dr Ali, and Global Effort — are natural hold-up types competing for the same rear-field berths. This field holds significantly more hold-up horses than can all settle where they want; Dr Ali, My Mate Mackley, and Global Effort are the three most likely to find themselves racing closer than their natural style dictates, with Real Gold and Zaltalla the most likely to secure genuine back-of-the-field positions. A controlled, single-pacemaker race on a flat AW track in Standard conditions historically rewards those who can travel close to the pace and kick off it — prominent racers and closers with tactical speed benefit most, while deep hold-up horses face an uphill task if Pure Passion never truly cranks the tempo up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Passion Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Passion settles uncontested in front and controls a steady-to-moderate tempo throughout the 6f.
scenarios.body: Pure Passion sets an unhurried pace, denying the field a strong gallop to aim at, and those sitting just behind her in prominent positions get the perfect tow into the straight before she tries to kick clear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Chase Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If Porfin and Roman Spring both press Pure Passion aggressively early and the pace lifts enough to stretch the field.
scenarios.body: The front trio race in a line, the pace becomes genuine, and Pure Passion's early advantage is neutralised in the final furlong as the prominent horses have the momentum to peg her back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough and held long enough that the true hold-up types — Zaltalla or Real Gold — can close from behind.
scenarios.body: With a steady-to-moderate gallop this is the less likely shape, but if the redistribution compresses the midfield and Zaltalla or Real Gold find clear runs, they can pick up late ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Surprise Result
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Passion is taken on unexpectedly and either fades badly or the whole field bunches into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A messy finish with no clear positional advantage; lower-rated horses like Global Effort or Dr Ali could fluke a placing if pace judgement breaks down completely.

watchPoints.text: Pure Passion's weight (137lbs) and unproven 6f stamina on AW-Standard are the two live risks — if she ties up inside the final furlong, Porfin and Roman Spring are best-placed to capitalise immediately.

Roman Spring's 5-day turnaround means watch the paddock and early behaviour; if the horse is flat or reluctant, its prominent position will be surrendered quickly and the scenario B probability collapses.

With Dr Ali, My Mate Mackley, and Global Effort all being true hold-up horses forced closer than they'd like, watch for traffic jams at the 2f pole — a bunched midfield increases the risk of interference and scrubbing.

Global Effort's 150-day absence is the longest of any runner; first-time-back horses at Lingfield AW over 6f can need the run, and Tyler Heard is an inexperienced conditional — monitor market moves late for any stable confidence signals.

Ridger's trainer Ollie Sangster has three runners in the T14 window (3/13), which is active for a yard with a horse showing three poor runs — if there is any market support, treat it as meaningful given the raw form offers little else.

races.name: Become A Friend Of Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Neswick
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly for Marcus Tregoning with David Probert up; has only one run to her name (placed over 10f on Standard) and 108 days off the track make her a significant unknown quantity, though the trip and going are familiar.|

runners_data.name: Oklahoma Dream
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's filly steps up to 1m2f having run twice on Standard, finishing fifth on both occasions; the hood (headgear) is a flag for attitude issues and she has not shown form to suggest she can win off this mark.|

runners_data.name: Paraone
runners_data.note: Heather Main debutante with Finley Marsh in the saddle and no runs to assess — going preference completely unknown, making her a pure wildcard whose natural style cannot be assessed from available data.|

runners_data.name: Protectrix
runners_data.note: John Butler's lightly-raced filly ran seventh over 7f on Standard last time; John Callan takes the ride, and stepping up considerably in trip is unproven, though the stable has a decent 14-day strike rate of 5/18.|

runners_data.name: Shangri La
runners_data.note: David Simcock's filly has course form over the trip but is a natural hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map because the field is top-heavy with closers; her STYLE_FIT flag tempers her chance, and OR 73 leaves her facing a stiff class task against 120-rated rivals.|

runners_data.name: Walking On Stars
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly is the race's confirmed pace-setter and will control the tempo from the front; the STYLE_FIT tag notes she is pressed to lead rather than prominent, but her natural dominance at this track and trip in a steady-gallop scenario makes her the pivotal horse — 14 days since last run is no concern for this yard.|

runners_data.name: Blue Hill
runners_data.note: Ismail Mohammed's filly tracked prominently when fourth over 11f on Standard and shapes as the most natural horse to sit second behind Walking On Stars; Benoit de la Sayette is an able pilot and the step back to 1m2f from her debut looks sensible.|

runners_data.name: Champagne Beau
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings' filly carries a "fades in finish" flag and ran eighth and ninth on her two starts on Good and Soft — Standard AW ground is new territory and there is no evidence she sees out further than 8f, making her an outsider.|

runners_data.name: Dove Tale
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden entry with Robert Havlin, who showed course form with a third over 11f on Standard; a natural hold-up horse dropping back slightly in trip, she is the most credentialled of the closers and Havlin's course knowledge is an asset.|

races.paceDynamic: Walking On Stars is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will settle into an uncontested, measured gallop on this 1m2f Lingfield AW trip — a sustainable pace that plays to her strengths without burning fuel. Blue Hill shapes as the likely second horse behind her, tracking prominently, while the hold-up contingent of Oklahoma Dream, Dove Tale, Shangri La, and Champagne Beau will settle towards the rear. Shangri La is tagged as redistributed — the field holds more natural hold-up types than can realistically fill those positions, and Walking On Stars and Blue Hill are the horses most likely to actually secure the early prominent berths. With the pace likely to be honest but controlled, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can control the tempo and outstay rivals in the straight, rather than late closers who will need a strong gallop to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Walking On Stars dictates an uncontested, measured pace and kicks clear in the straight unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Walking On Stars benefits from a solo lead with no pressure, conserving energy before asserting in the final two furlongs on a track and trip that suits her style; Blue Hill, tracking close throughout, is best-placed to pick up any weakness.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pull Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Hill matches strides with Walking On Stars throughout and the pair distance the hold-up horses in the straight.
scenarios.body: The early gallop is shared between two prominent types, setting a rhythm that holds off late challengers who lack the closing burst to reel them in on a Standard surface; Dove Tale, closest of the hold-up horses, may grab a piece of the action.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the leaders tie each other up, leaving room for hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Dove Tale, showing course form at the trip, and Oklahoma Dream, whose headgear suggests a sharper profile, would be best-positioned to close if the front pair overcook it; this scenario requires a pace genuinely honest enough to drain the front runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Finish, Held Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the middle stages and a patient hold-up horse outstays a flat-footed field.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Walking On Stars' natural front-running style and the lack of serious pace pressure, but Dove Tale — who has Gosden form and handles Standard — would be the primary beneficiary; Shangri La, though racing out of her natural role, carries fitness from a recent run 30 days ago.

watchPoints.text: Walking On Stars sets the entire pace map — if she breaks cleanly and gets to the front uncontested, everything depends on whether the hold-up horses can run her down in the straight, which on this gallop they likely cannot.

Dove Tale is the one hold-up horse with proven Standard AW course form over a similar trip; watch how Havlin positions her in the first three furlongs, as any gap in the field could see her make a bold move.
Paraone is a complete unknown on debut — if she shows natural speed and troubles Walking On Stars for the lead, the pace dynamic changes materially and the whole race shape shifts.

Champagne Beau's "fades in finish" flag and soft/good-ground form make her a horse to watch for signs of backing off in the straight — her behaviour under pressure could illuminate whether the Standard surface is an issue for others in the field too.

Shangri La's redistribution from hold-up to midfield means Callum Shepherd may find himself in an unfamiliar tactical position; watch whether he pushes forward or drops back, as either move will tell you how the stable reads her chance today.

runners_data.name: Wolf's Gallop
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's runner has been consistent in placing without winning, finishing 3rd-3rd-4th on Good, and steps back to the 5f trip it handles well; naturally prominent and should secure a clean tracking position just behind the speed if the pace battle ahead plays out as expected.
runners_data.comment: Placed third in two of his last four starts, Wolf's Gallop arrives here on a sharp 15-day turnaround and has run over today's trip, with our rating of 80 setting him apart from his rivals; yet to win in recent starts, but the form profile makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Beautiful Effort
runners_data.note: Ismail Mohammed's filly has no wins or places on Standard going from three attempts at the track and distance combination, making her going profile a genuine concern; she wants to race prominently but with four rivals ahead of her in the queue she may find herself wider and further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with finishes of fifth, sixth, and ninth, Beautiful Effort faces a stiff ask here — though she has run over today's trip and returns after 36 days carrying 128 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Sultan Darius
runners_data.note: Marco Botti has had two winners from 15 runners in the past fortnight suggesting yard is in reasonable nick; Sultan Darius has placed twice from three starts over 5-6f on Good and racing with a hood, he is a natural prominent runner who should get a position close enough to the pace to challenge if it collapses.
runners_data.comment: Sultan Darius has run over today's trip and returns on a good 21-day break, with two fourths in his last three starts suggesting he's knocking on the door — the eighth sandwiched between them is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Stoney Wood
runners_data.note: Trainer Michael Bell sends this filly back to 5f after three runs at 6f, a distance reduction that makes some appeal, but the horse has faded in the finish in her last two runs and the ⚠ fade flag makes her hard to trust off a strongly-run pace even with the trip shortening.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and drawn six carrying 126 lb, Stoney Wood has run over today's distance and going before, though a struggling trainer strike-rate of 5% over the past fortnight gives his prospects a further dampener.

runners_data.name: Miss Moneypit
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly has a win to her name over 5f on Good and a respectable placed record in similar grades, and her true style is pressing the pace — however, with multiple rivals ahead of her in the race shape, she is likely to end up in a position further back than she wants, which tempers her chance meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Miss Moneypit won two starts back and returns on a sharp 12-day turnaround with distance experience in her favour, and her rating of 76 suggests she holds strong claims from stall one — though last time's fourth will need reversing.

runners_data.name: From Me To You
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's hold-up runner has just one placing from four runs on Standard going and posted a notable 23rd-of-field run last time on Good; the tongue tie is noted but with a weak recent form string and poor sim-going record this is a low-confidence runner even if the pace does collapse.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with an unplaced effort the most recent of them, From Me To You is hard to fancy on these figures — ranked eighth of nine — though he has run over today's trip before and 26 days between runs leaves him fresh.

runners_data.name: Secret Rival
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's front-runner has the lowest OR in the field at 62 but is a confirmed pace-setter and will likely push hard for the lead from gate to wire; the risk is she burns bright early and ties up in the straight, but she gives the race its shape and must not be ignored for place purposes if she gets a soft lead for a few strides.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with finishes of eighth, sixth, and seventh in that run of form, Secret Rival has little recent encouragement to offer; she has run over today's trip before and 28 days between runs suggests freshness, but she ranks last on our figures here.

runners_data.name: South West
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's juvenile has the highest OR at 75, won over 5f on Good last time, and is the most likely horse to emerge from the pace battle in front; blinkers applied, Finley Marsh takes the ride, and the horse's raw class advantage over rivals on OR could make it very hard to peg back if it settles near the front.
runners_data.comment: South West arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, making him a clear danger at 135 lb from stall 5; the sole risk is whether that victory came against stronger opposition than he'll face here.

runners_data.name: American Psycho
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's hold-up runner has the second-highest OR at 74 and has placed twice from three starts including a second on Good over 5f; his Standard going record is 0 wins and 0 places from three attempts which is a mild flag, but the class and consistent proximity to the leaders make this the most credible late challenger if the pace burns hot enough.

runners_data.name: Viking Barbie
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's filly has been placed in four of four starts with a second and two thirds over 5f on Good, displaying admirable consistency; returning after 41 days, Daniel Muscutt rides and she is a natural prominent runner who will try to secure a handy position — but with so many rivals fighting for that space she may get bumped further back at a crucial stage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts but has shown consistency through a second and a third in that sequence; she has run over today's trip and her 131 lb burden from stall seven keeps her competitive, though she'll need to find more to threaten at the finish.

races.paceDynamic: South West and Secret Rival are both confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the off on this flat Lingfield AW 5f, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than an uncontested canter — the gallop will be honest and possibly sharp from the gates. Wolf's Gallop, Sultan Darius, Viking Barbie, and Beautiful Effort all want to race prominently, meaning there is a dangerous cluster of four horses hunting the same positions two or three furlongs out, creating a high risk of traffic issues mid-race. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the shape can comfortably accommodate — South West is best placed to actually command the lead given the highest OR and a course-suitable win last time, with Sultan Darius and Wolf's Gallop most likely to secure genuine prominent berths ahead of Viking Barbie and Beautiful Effort who may be shuffled back under pressure. The tactical verdict is clear: a contested but honest pace over 5f on a flat AW track favours runners who can travel smoothly just off the speed and sustain their effort through the final furlong, putting prominent-to-midfield closers with a clean passage — particularly those with proven Standard going form — in the strongest position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If South West and Secret Rival fight for the lead and honest fractions allow a prominent racer travelling smoothly to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Wolf's Gallop and Sultan Darius are ideally placed to track the speed and benefit as the two pace-setters potentially tie each other up, hitting the line with residual energy while the leaders fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If South West shakes off Secret Rival early and is allowed to bowl along at a controlled tempo, controlling fractions through the straight.
scenarios.body: South West has the highest OR in the field, won over 5f on Good last time, and if able to find a comfortable lead could simply prove too strong for rivals chasing from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle between South West and Secret Rival burns fiercely enough to open the race up for genuine hold-up horses coming late.
scenarios.body: American Psycho is the most credible closer with a second from four on this surface profile and a trainer in Archie Watson who excels with improving juveniles; From Me To You and Stoney Wood have less encouraging profiles but benefit from maximum pace collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If crowding 2-3f out causes interference that reshuffles the entire field and the race turns into a sprint finish from the dip.
scenarios.body: In a chaotic finish Viking Barbie's consistent placed form and Daniel Muscutt's positional awareness give it an each-way foothold, while Miss Moneypit — a genuine prominent type who may find clear daylight in a scrappy finish — could outrun her mapped position.

watchPoints.text: South West and Secret Rival are on a direct collision course for the lead — watch for an aggressive early duel that could cause crowding on the inside rail in the first two furlongs, affecting Wolf's Gallop and Sultan Darius who want to be handy.

Viking Barbie, Beautiful Effort, and Miss Moneypit are all chasing the same prominent positions in a field with more pace than it can absorb — traffic danger between 3f and 2f out is elevated and any rider unable to find clear daylight will lose their chance abruptly.

American Psycho's Standard going record is 0-from-3 with no place, which is a quiet concern for a horse whose scenario depends on the race setting up perfectly for a late run — if the pace is honest rather than brutal, this runner may not get close enough.

Stoney Wood is flagged as fading in the finish; watch whether Callum Shepherd tries to drop her out and ride for a more economical run, or whether the trip drop to 5f prompts a more forward approach — either way the fade flag reduces confidence in the final 100 yards.

Miss Moneypit won over 5f on Good and is naturally a front-pace horse, but mapped to midfield due to pace congestion — if she gets shuffled wide or loses her footing in traffic early she may never reach her best position, discounting her chance even more than the style-fit tag suggests.
